title: Gift Wrap Roll

drivers.name: Price increase (2.5%)
drivers.evidence: Price rose from 5.39 to 5.53. Past promotions show no consistent lift at this price point; one 30% off saw only x0.95 lift. Price increases tend to reduce demand. Noise-adjusted estimate for price impact is x0.85, so -15% effect.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 4.1. No event is scheduled for the target week. The price is up 2.5% vs regular, which historically reduces demand. Past promotions show a median lift of x1.54, but noise-adjusted effect is x1.0. The week after a promotion typically sees x0.84 (noise-adjusted x1.0). The target week is not after a promotion. Mother's Day is next week, but the prior week (this week) is not a driver. Price increase suggests downside. No evidence of lift. The classical model suggests no change. Confidence is medium due to sparse past promotion data and price effect not well measured.

brief:
PRODUCT: Gift Wrap Roll | category Seasonal | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-04-27 to 2026-05-03 (next week)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 5.53 (+2.5% vs regular price 5.39)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 4.1 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 10.7 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 8.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-97% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
